result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by a large elevated steel structure and a wide multi-lane roadway. While marked crosswalks and pedestrian signals are present, the scale of the infrastructure and the presence of large support pillars create a complex environment with significant visual obstructions.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Infrastructure
hazards.description: Large steel support pillars for the elevated structure are located on the sidewalk near the intersection, significantly blocking sightlines between turning drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right foreground and middle ground along the sidewalk edge

hazards.name: Wide Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The multi-lane roadway requires pedestrians to cross a significant distance, increasing their exposure time to vehicle traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image across the main roadway

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to reduce the crossing distance and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight beyond the support pillars.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to provide a 3-7 second head start for pedestrians before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Enhance the existing median into a protected refuge island to allow pedestrians to cross the wide street in two stages.

result.summary: The image shows a midblock pedestrian crossing adjacent to an institutional building, marked with paint and a warning sign. While a continuous sidewalk is present, the environment lacks physical traffic calming or a buffer between pedestrians and the roadway.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Midblock Crossing
hazards.description: A marked crossing without signals or physical calming increases the risk of vehicle-pedestrian conflicts, especially near a school/community center.
hazards.location_in_image: Center left, where the crosswalk markings and pedestrian sign are located.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the travel lane with no physical separation or parked cars to protect pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground sidewalk along the bottom of the image.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised island in the center of the roadway to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time and reduce exposure.

interventions.title: Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon (RRFB)
interventions.description: Add user-actuated amber LEDs to the crossing signs to significantly increase driver yielding rates at this midblock location.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the roadway at the crossing to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The street is a wide, multi-lane corridor with continuous sidewalks but lacks pedestrian-specific safety features like marked crossings or buffers. The environment is dominated by vehicle traffic, with a long blank fence on one side and parallel parking on the other, creating a functional but uninviting pedestrian experience.

hazards.name: Wide Roadway
hazards.description: The multi-lane configuration encourages higher vehicle speeds and increases the distance pedestrians must cross without protection.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image

hazards.name: Lack of Sidewalk Buffer
hazards.description: Pedestrians on the left sidewalk are separated from moving traffic only by a standard curb, increasing risk from vehicle incursions.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image

hazards.name: Blank Frontage
hazards.description: The long fence on the left side creates a monotonous environment with no passive surveillance, reducing pedestrian comfort.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image

interventions.title: Lane Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce the width of travel lanes to naturally slow vehicle speeds and provide space for other uses like a bike lane or wider buffer.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised island in the center of the roadway to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time safely.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Landscaping
interventions.description: Add a planting strip with trees between the sidewalk and the curb to provide a physical buffer and improve the microclimate.

result.summary: The image depicts a wide urban arterial road adjacent to an elevated rail structure and a large commercial storage facility. While sidewalks and marked crosswalks are present, the multi-lane configuration and industrial scale of the environment suggest a focus on vehicle throughput over pedestrian comfort.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Infrastructure
hazards.description: The large support pillars for the elevated rail structure create significant blind spots for both drivers and pedestrians at the intersection.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image, where the elevated rail meets the street level.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The multi-lane roadway requires pedestrians to cross a significant distance without a refuge island, increasing exposure to traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and right foreground, across the main roadway.

hazards.name: Driveway Conflict Point
hazards.description: A wide curb cut for the U-Haul facility creates a point where vehicles may cross the pedestrian walkway unexpectedly.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image, in front of the U-Haul building.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade the standard parallel line crosswalks to high-visibility continental markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to reduce the crossing distance and improve sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.
